text: Welcome to the version 1.6 walkthrough. It shows the changes asked for after the management review: one master workbook, depots instead of C F A, customer types and codes, the invoice recognition code, and local autos charged per trip or per box. The database is empty. Every record you will see is a demonstration entry.
title: CTDMS Version 1.6 - Master's Walkthrough

text: This is the dashboard of a brand-new installation. The menu now says Depot wherever it used to say C F A, and all the master records live under Master Settings.
First, one more person: a checker, because rates still need a second person's approval.
Step one. On the first day, all the master data compiled from MARG, SAP, CBO and Intrect is uploaded once, in one cleaned workbook.
title: Step 1 - One master workbook

text: Master Settings, Initial Master Upload. The blank workbook can be downloaded here. Its first sheet explains every column; the other sheets are companies, depots, customers, customer types, transporters, locations, local auto rates, freight rates, invoice code mappings and E R P mappings. Product and S K U sheets are not part of version one point six.
We upload the demonstration workbook. Nothing is saved yet: CTDMS first checks every row.

The preview gives accepted and rejected counts for each sheet. Four rows have problems, and each one says why: a depot without a city, a customer typed twice, a customer whose delivery location does not exist, and the Retailer customer type, which already exists in CTDMS and is therefore skipped, not duplicated.
Only the valid rows will be imported. We press Import.

Fifty two master records were created in one go. The rejected rows stay in the history with an Excel error report, so they can be corrected. From now on, single new records are added under Master Settings.
Step two. A quick look at the masters the workbook created.
title: Step 2 - What the workbook created

text: The Company Master. Each company keeps its code and has a short recognition code: A B C, X Y Z, P Q R and T D L for our own distribution. Each is linked to its billing system.
The Depot Master. Raipur has two depots, Guma and Kamal Vihar. They are in the same city but are separate depots, each with its own code, locality and recognition code. Bilaspur has its own depot.
Inside a depot: locality, city, address, the companies it handles and its usual billing system.

Customer Types are now a master of their own, not fixed in the program: retailer, stockist, distributor, hospital, institution, chain pharmacy, other, plus the two the workbook added. Each has a short code, like R E T. Notice that Government Supply has no code yet. We will come back to that.
The Customer Master: customer code, name, customer type, recognition code like C zero two five, delivery location and the companies served.
Each customer also keeps its source E R P and the code that E R P uses, so imports find the customer automatically.
Long-distance transporters work exactly as in version one point five: a rate card per area, L R numbers and a monthly bill.
Local autos are listed separately. Sharma Local Auto charges per trip, usually five hundred rupees. Ravi Tempo charges per box. Kishore Mini Truck can be charged either way.
Per-box rates can depend on the location, the company and the depot. Ravi Tempo charges twenty rupees a box in Raipur, twenty five to Bhilai, and twenty two for P Q R's goods in Raipur.

Invoice Code Mappings hold the markings our billing systems already put in their invoice numbers. In MARG, an invoice starting with X Y slash G is X Y Z Healthcare from the Guma depot; X Y slash K is from Kamal Vihar.
The freight rates from the workbook wait for the checker. The checker reviews them and presses Approve all. The person who uploaded them could not approve them.
Step three. After the first day, nobody re-uploads the whole workbook. A new record is simply added in Master Settings.
title: Step 3 - Adding a record later

text: A new local auto has joined: Mohan's e-rickshaw, charged per trip, usually three hundred rupees.
It is saved, and it will be in the local auto list on the gatepass straight away.
Step four, the new provision: one internal code that tells, at a glance, which company, customer type, customer and depot an invoice belongs to.
title: Step 4 - Invoice Recognition Code

text: The code is built from the short codes in the masters: company, customer type, customer, depot, and the number part of the E R P invoice number. For example A B C, R E T, C zero two five, GUMA, then zero zero one two four five. The pattern can be changed here, and the whole feature can be switched off. The original invoice number is never touched.
Step five. Invoices arrive from the billing systems, and CTDMS recognises everything it can from the masters.
title: Step 5 - Invoices arrive

text: A B C Pharma's SAP export. The plant column tells the depot, through the E R P mapping from the workbook, and SAP's own customer numbers find our customers. All six rows are valid.
X Y Z Healthcare's MARG file has no company or depot column at all. The marking X Y slash G or X Y slash K in each bill number tells CTDMS both the company and the depot.
And P Q R Lifesciences from CBO, recognised the same way.

The Invoice Register now shows two numbers side by side. On the left, the original E R P invoice number, exactly as it came. Next to it, the Invoice Recognition Code. Company, depot, customer and customer type are all identified.

Here is invoice zero zero one two four five from SAP. Its number is unchanged. Its recognition code is A B C dash R E T dash C zero two five dash GUMA dash zero zero one two four five: A B C Pharma, a retailer, customer C zero two five, from the Guma depot.
One invoice could not get a code. The reason is clear: the customer type Government Supply has no recognition code. CTDMS does not guess. The invoice can still be dispatched normally.
We give Government Supply the code G O V in Master Settings and save.
The code is made at once: A B C dash G O V dash C zero nine zero dash B S P, then the invoice number.
Because every code starts with the same parts, searching is simple. Typing A B C dash R E T lists every A B C Pharma invoice to retailers.
Filtering by the city Raipur brings both Raipur depots together, Guma and Kamal Vihar. The depot filter would show just one of them.
Step six, dispatch. First the normal long-distance transporter, which works exactly as before.
title: Step 6 - Dispatch

text: Three invoices from the Bilaspur depot go with Shree Roadlines, a long-distance transporter. Freight comes from its rate card for each area, and Shree Roadlines will send its bill later.
Printed, out of the gate, L R numbers entered later. Nothing changed in this part.
Step seven. A local auto charged per trip.
title: Step 7 - Local auto, per trip

text: Sharma Local Auto takes four invoices from the Guma depot to customers in Raipur: five, fifteen, six and four boxes.

The operator types the actual trip charge, five hundred rupees today. It could be four fifty or five fifty on another day. The total stays five hundred: one trip, one amount. It is not five hundred times four invoices.
For the M I S, the five hundred is shared by boxes: about eighty three, two hundred and fifty, one hundred, and sixty seven rupees. The shares always add up to five hundred.
The dispatch slip prints the trip charge once, for the whole trip, with each invoice's original number and its recognition code.
Step eight. A local auto charged per box.
title: Step 8 - Local auto, per box

text: Ravi Tempo charges per box. From the Kamal Vihar depot, the operator first adds an invoice for Durg as well.
CTDMS warns that Ravi Tempo has no per-box rate for Durg. That invoice is taken off this trip.
Now: fifteen boxes at twenty rupees is three hundred, and six boxes of P Q R's goods at its own rate of twenty two is one hundred and thirty two. Total four hundred and thirty two rupees.
Kishore Mini Truck can be charged either way, so both choices appear. Today it is per trip, five hundred and fifty rupees, for one invoice to Bhilai.
Last step: the reports management sees.
title: Step 9 - Reports and MIS

text: The Local Auto Trips report. One row per trip. The amount owed to the auto, and the amount booked on its invoices, are always equal. The four-invoice trip shows five hundred rupees, not two thousand. Nothing is counted twice.
City-wise freight puts Guma and Kamal Vihar together under Raipur.
Depot-wise freight shows each depot separately, with its city.

Every invoice report shows the original E R P invoice number and the Invoice Recognition Code in separate columns, together with company, depot, city, customer type, boxes and transportation expense. All of it exports to Excel, C S V or P D F.
And the dashboard now shows the figures, including freight by depot with each depot's city.

That completes version one point six: one master workbook, depots with several in one city, customer types and codes, the invoice recognition code beside the unchanged E R P number, and local autos charged per trip or per box without double counting. Thank you.
title: End of the version 1.6 walkthrough
